bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent tops App Store, launches Shopify/PayPal checkout, triggers CPU rally
bullets.body: Meta's Muse personal AI agent reached #1 on the iOS App Store with ~3.1M downloads in 15 days—outpacing ChatGPT's launch—driving META +11% on 9/22, its best day in 17 months. Shopify CEO Tobi Lutke announced a commerce partnership enabling Muse agentic checkout via Shop Pay, while Amazon blocked Muse citing unauthorized access/credential capture. CPU and memory stocks (INTC +12%, AMD +10%, ARM +17%) rallied sharply on agentic AI infrastructure demand; META's May Connect event on 9/23-24 is expected to unveil Muse Charm device and VR glasses at $1,299. Multiple sell-side firms raised PTs: JPM to $920 (26x 2028E EPS), Piper to $875 OW, Mizuho OW at $750.

bullets.title: AKAM: $11.6B Anthropic deal transforms company from value to hypergrowth; multiple analysts raise PTs
bullets.body: Akamai announced the largest contract in company history—an $11.6B, 7-year take-or-pay deal with Anthropic for CPU-based cloud infrastructure (expandable to $20B), driving AKAM +15-23% in a single session. Deal economics average $22M/MW vs. GPU deals; requires ~$5.5B capex ($1.7B 4Q26, $3.1B 2027) with no GPU requirement. Revenue ramps 2H27 to $150-300M for FY27, reaching ~$1.7B annual run-rate by YE28. JPM raised PT to $167 (Neutral on 93% Anthropic concentration risk); Oppenheimer OW $180; DA Davidson Buy $185; Piper OW $158.

bullets.title: ORCL: Force majeure on Project Jupiter roils AI infrastructure financing; Mizuho and KeyBanc maintain constructive
bullets.body: Oracle invoked force majeure on the 2.45GW Project Jupiter New Mexico data center (part of the $400B OpenAI/SoftBank Stargate initiative) to defer payments if site misses its 2028 launch—triggered by natural gas pipeline permitting delays. Project debt traded below 90 cents. Oracle denied the project is off-schedule; Mizuho (Outperform) notes no FY27 guidance impact and reiterates Investor Day on 10/28 as key catalyst; KeyBanc (OW, $300 PT) flags ORCL's cash position as the most tenuous among hyperscalers. BE, which has a $1.25B EBITDA take-or-pay contract for Jupiter fuel cells, saw its stock fall in sympathy but MS kept FY27 shipment forecasts intact given contractual protections.

bullets.title: CMCSA: KeyBanc downgrades to Underweight, $18 PT; Morgan Stanley cuts PT on AI agent broadband risk
bullets.body: KeyBanc downgraded Comcast to Underweight (from Sector Weight) with an $18 PT, citing worsening broadband churn as competitors offer $30-40/month 1Gbps packages, soft Orlando theme park attendance, and no spin-off catalyst. 3Q broadband net adds expected at -140K to -160K vs. consensus -119K to -172K. Morgan Stanley separately cut CMCSA PT to $27 from $29 and CHTR PT to $140 from $150, citing AI agent-driven ARPU deflation risk; TMUS remains MS top pick as least-exposed, while T upgraded to $28.

bullets.title: MU: Q4 consensus $31.52 EPS / $51B revenue; Wolfe and UBS model 7x+ thru-cycle upside
bullets.body: Micron reports September 30 after close (consensus: $31.52 EPS, $50.97B revenue). Wolfe stays Outperform with $1,500 PT, projecting DRAM/HBM pricing strength into CY28 and MU capable of buying back 25-32% of market cap in CY26-27. UBS models C2027-29E EPS of $212/$277/$219 well above Street, with HBM ASPs rising ~76% YoY; CHIPS Act buyback restriction expires 12/9/26 with $20-50B/Q repos thereafter. ITC instituted a patent investigation against MU on four NLST DRAM patents—analyst expects additional licensing agreements to follow.

bullets.title: AMD: Joins $1T market cap club on agentic-AI CPU demand thesis; earnings beat expectations
bullets.body: AMD crossed $1 trillion market cap on 9/22/26, driven by the narrative that agentic AI workloads require 3-4 CPUs per GPU vs. 7-8 for training, dramatically expanding CPU TAM. Stock is up ~290% YTD and hit all-time highs during the week. Citi and Piper maintain Outperform ratings, noting AMD's EPYC Venice positioned for agentic AI; Hedgeye confirmed bullish TREND breakout. GS rates AMD Neutral vs. Buy on ARM; INTC also surged +12% on the same CPU narrative.

bullets.title: TSEM: Mizuho initiates Outperform, $300 PT on silicon photonics leadership and 60% CAGR optical market
bullets.body: Mizuho initiated Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) at Outperform with a $300 price target, citing TSEM as the leading foundry for silicon photonics chips. The optical connectivity market is forecast at ~$8.5B by F29E (60% 4-year CAGR); RF Infrastructure revenue expected to grow 76% CAGR to 77% of total revenue by FY29E, with gross margin expanding from 23% to 50% and EPS growing ~7x. The $300 PT implies 0.6x F27E PEG, below peers' 0.9x. TSEM was also included in StreetAccount's 52-week highs on 9/25.

bullets.title: CRWV: JPM upgrades to Overweight, $125 PT on short-dated GPU contract pricing power
bullets.body: JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight with a $125 PT (was Neutral, $120), citing July GPU pricing +25% across SKUs with short-term contract pricing at ~3x longer-term rates. Margins expanding from 1% trough in F1Q26 to guidance low-teens by F4Q26 and 20-25% long-term. >75% of $30B+ exit-2027 ARR already contracted. UBS also initiated CRWV at Buy ($120 PT). Non-GPU adjacencies (storage, CPU, networking) exceeded $400M ARR in F2Q26.

bullets.title: PSKY/WBD: Paramount settles antitrust suit with state AGs; merger set to close in ~2 weeks
bullets.body: Paramount Skydance reached settlement with California and other state AGs, clearing the path for the $110B WBD acquisition with no structural divestitures. Settlement requires 30-32 theatrical releases/year, $1.5B incremental US production spend, and $300M annual investment. Morgan Stanley raised PSKY PT to $11.50 (OW); Sean Diffley sees path to $8B FCF and >240M subs by 2030 (potential for combined HBO Max + Paramount+ to rank 2nd/3rd behind Netflix). WBD and PSKY each rallied ~7-11% on the news.

bullets.title: MRVL: MS raises PT to $268; interconnect revenue now tracking >70% YoY growth
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised Marvell's PT to $268 from $246 (now 49x CY27E EPS) at its EU Semis coverage day, citing greater confidence in the longer-term AI upside. Oppenheimer's road-notes show MRVL scale-across revenue on track to top $1B next year and interconnect is growing >70% YoY vs prior 50% expectations. Marvell's Investor Day is scheduled for October 6, where the company is expected to raise FY2030 revenue guidance above $40B. Seaport Research initiated MRVL Buy at $270.

bullets.title: VRT: Wells Fargo initiates Overweight; stock diverges from MOD after Semianalysis data-center concern note
bullets.body: Wells Fargo initiated Vertiv at Overweight in pre-market on 9/25, driving the stock +2.5% at open. However, VRT had underperformed meaningfully since a 9/9 Semianalysis note raising data-center equipment concerns—down 16% vs. MOD +4% since then. OPCO noted the divergence in its industrials commentary, viewing the valuation gap as a potential opportunity. Morgan Stanley's OW thesis on VRT ($33 PT) centers on consumer agent infrastructure tailwinds.

bullets.title: CIEN: Evercore upgrades to Outperform, PT $550 from $375; optical networking themes dominate ECOC
bullets.body: Evercore ISI upgraded Ciena to Outperform with a $550 PT (raised from $375), citing AI-driven optical networking demand with a projected 24% market CAGR to $52B by FY2029 and CIEN EPS expected above $25. At the ECOC 2026 conference, CIEN management indicated revenue would exceed $8B if supply were unconstrained; company is targeting $10B+ backlog at fiscal year-end. Multiple LITE and COHR takeaways were also constructive: LITE NPO sole-sourced on a higher-port-count inference SKU; COHR unveiled PhotonLink platform with 10+ CPO, NPO, and chip-to-chip engagements.

bullets.title: DKNG: Massachusetts AI examination and elevated Predictions spend weigh on stock
bullets.body: Massachusetts gambling regulators announced they would examine how DraftKings and other betting companies use AI—driving DKNG -2.4% in pre-market on 9/25. Oppenheimer separately revised Predictions investments from $200-300M to $400-500M, lowering FY26E EBITDA 20% to $548M vs. prior $700-900M guidance. September MTD handle tracking +15% YoY supports core-EBITDA heading toward $1B, maintaining Outperform thesis.

bullets.title: FOXA/ROKU: UBS raises FOXA F1Q Tubi estimates to +25% YoY; Wedbush sees $400M+ in deal synergies
bullets.body: UBS raised F1Q Tubi estimates to 25% YoY growth (prior 17%) and lifted F1Q EBITDA to $1.37B (+~30% YoY) for Fox Corp, maintaining Buy with $4.1B FY27 EBITDA guidance unchanged. Wedbush noted Fox-Roku deal likely approved by regulators in 1H27 with $400M+ in identified run-rate cost synergies, calling the combined entity more valuable than parts. The ad market is benefiting from football, elections, and streaming-to-linear rotation.

bullets.title: MSFT: Stifel upgrades to Buy, $575 PT; Copilot discounts launched ahead of 'Super App' rollout
bullets.body: Stifel upgraded Microsoft to Buy (from Hold) and raised its PT to $575, citing Azure at ~46% CC growth in FQ1 and approaching 50% with new capacity, plus Copilot monetization broadening from seat-based to agent-driven consumption. MSFT launched 30-50% Copilot corporate discounts and introduced Home, Code, and Autopilot personal-agent capabilities. McCullough's Hedgeye also flipped MSFT from bearish to bullish TREND. Oppenheimer raised PT to $570 from $515. Hedgeye Risk Range signals MSFT bullish at buy $488, sell $507.

bullets.title: ACN: JPM raises PT to $200 on FY27 M&A contribution; UBS upgrades to Buy on AWS collaboration
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised its December-27 PT on Accenture to $200 (from $179) despite lowering FY27 EPS to $14.41 from $14.66, citing $5B in incremental Q4 debt to fund acquisitions (250bps M&A growth contribution). Separately, UBS upgraded ACN to Buy with a $275 PT, citing the launch of Accenture Edge (targeting $300M-$3B companies) with six AWS Marketplace offerings across AI, cloud security, and FinOps. FY27 revenue guidance expected at +2-5% CC with ~1% organic at midpoint.

bullets.title: NOK/Optical: Jefferies BUY NOK at €13.80 PT; new InP fab to drive 20x+ capacity expansion
bullets.body: Jefferies upgraded Nokia's optical segment to BUY with an €13.80 PT (from €9.28, +49%), citing NOK's internal InP integration providing a cost structural advantage and €5B+ in optical orders from AI customers since 2025. A second San Jose InP fab is coming online in 2026, increasing capacity more than 20x when fully ramped, with an additional NXP fab being acquired for Scale Across, DCI, and Scale Up/Out. Jefferies' 2027-28 EPS forecasts are ~21% above consensus. Nokia gained 13% in a single week after returning to the SX5E index.

bullets.title: NFLX: HSBC downgrades to Hold, cuts PT to $76; bearish on AI agent subscription disruption
bullets.body: HSBC downgraded Netflix to Hold (from Buy) and cut its price target to $76 from $96—below FactSet consensus of $93. The downgrade reflects concerns about subscription model disruption from AI agents automating cancellation workflows, pricing pressure from 'streamflation,' and slowing growth. Morgan Stanley's agentic AI framework separately flags SIRI as most exposed among subscription platforms, while primary ticketing and live entertainment (LYV, SPHR, TKO) benefit as spending is redirected to experiences.

bullets.title: AXTI: S&P SmallCap 600 inclusion drives 12%+ rally; flagged as InP substrate bottleneck play
bullets.body: AXT Inc. (AXTI) surged 12.4% on 9/22 following inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 (effective 9/21), triggering passive buying. Multiple semiconductor analysts flagged AXTI as a strategic holding tied to InP substrate supply—a key bottleneck for US AI optical infrastructure. Premarket data on 9/25 showed AXTI down 3.3% with no new catalyst, suggesting index-flow impact fading. Author at Photon Capital noted COHR has already made a prepayment to AXTI, signaling supply commitment.

bullets.title: RCL: Acquiring 50% stake in Sandals/Beaches Resorts for ~$3B; JPM upgrades on TAM expansion
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean confirmed acquisition of a 50% stake in Sandals and Beaches Resorts for ~$3B (~10x forward EBITDA), expanding its total addressable market from cruise into the $35B global all-inclusive TAM. JPMorgan upgraded RCL and raised PT; UBS (Buy, $367 PT) views the deal as EPS/EBITDA accretive in 2027 with only ~0.3x leverage impact. The deal includes 18-20 Caribbean resorts with 5,062 rooms and 30% customer overlap with existing cruise guests. RCL was at 52-week lows before the announcement on broader sector weakness.
